sentences: An invitation to dinner was soon afterwards despatched; and already had Mrs. Bennet planned the courses that were to do credit to her housekeeping, when an answer arrived which deferred it all.

Elizabeth made no answer, and took her place in the set, amazed at the dignity to which she was arrived in being allowed to stand opposite to Mr. Darcy, and reading in her neighbours' looks their equal amazement in beholding it.
The garden sloping to the road, the house standing in it, the green pales and the laurel hedge, everything declared they were arriving.

The time fixed for the beginning of their northern tour was now fast approaching; and a fortnight only was wanting of it, when a letter arrived from Mrs. Gardiner, which at once delayed its commencement and curtailed its extent.
When Mr. Bennet arrived, he had all the appearance of his usual philosophic composure.
It was all over before I arrived; so my curiosity was not so dreadfully racked as yours seems to have been.

senses.gloss: reach a destination; arrive by movement or progress
senses.learner: to get to the place you were going to
examples: When Mr. Bennet arrived, he had all the appearance of his usual philosophic composure.
a letter arrived from Mrs. Gardiner

senses.gloss: succeed in a big way; get to the top
senses.learner: to become very successful and reach the top
examples: After years of small parts, she felt she had finally arrived.

sentences: They always continue to grow sufficiently unlike afterwards to have their share of vexation; and it is better to know as little as possible of the defects of the person with whom you are to pass your life."

senses.learner: a fault in someone or something, or a lack of something that is needed.

it is better to know as little as possible of the defects of the person with whom you are to pass your life

senses.gloss: an imperfection in an object or machine

sentences: Her mind was less difficult to develope.
Among those who are at all his equals in consequence, he is a very different man from what he is to the less prosperous.

Jane confessed herself a little surprised at the match: but she said less of her astonishment than of her earnest desire for their happiness; nor could Elizabeth persuade her to consider it as improbable.
Mr. Darcy, who was leaning against the mantel-piece with his eyes fixed on her face, seemed to catch her words with no less resentment than surprise.
The walk being here less sheltered than on the other side, allowed them to see him before they met.
I am glad of one thing, that he comes alone; because we shall see the less of him.

senses.gloss: (comparative of ‘little’ usually used with mass nouns) a quantifier meaning not as great in amount or degree
senses.learner: not as much in amount or degree.
examples: she said less of her astonishment than of her earnest desire for their happiness
There was less noise in the room after they left.

senses.gloss: (nonstandard in some uses but often idiomatic with measure phrases) fewer
examples: The whole journey took less than three hours.

senses.learner: lower in quality; usually used after the word 'no'.
examples: She would take nothing less than his best work.

sentences: "I beg you will not put it into Lizzy's head to be vexed by his ill-treatment, for he is such a disagreeable man that it would be quite a misfortune to be liked by him.
That would be the greatest misfortune of all!
repeated Darcy, contemptuously,--"yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed."
But the misfortune of speaking with bitterness is a most natural consequence of the prejudices I had been encouraging.

The Bennets were speedily pronounced to be the luckiest family in the world; though only a few weeks before, when Lydia had first run away, they had been generally proved to be marked out for misfortune.

senses.gloss: unnecessary and unforeseen trouble resulting from an unfortunate event
senses.learner: trouble that did not have to happen and that no one saw coming, brought on by an unlucky event.
examples: yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed
No arguments shall be wanting on my part, that can alleviate so severe a misfortune

senses.gloss: an unfortunate state resulting from unfavorable outcomes
senses.learner: a bad situation you are in because things have turned out badly.
examples: they had been generally proved to be marked out for misfortune
Years of misfortune had worn the family down.
